Education & Research

How to Check a Breast Surgeon’s Credentials in India

Choosing the surgeon is one of the most important decisions in any breast procedure. In India, a doctor can legally practise medicine without being a trained plastic surgeon, so it is worth checking carefully.

Home/Education & Research/How to Check a Breast Surgeon’s Credentials in India

This page is general guidance. Rules change, so verify details with official sources and the relevant professional body.

1. Check medical registration

A doctor should be registered with the National Medical Commission or a State Medical Council. Ask for their registration number and check it on the official register.

2. Check specialist training

Ask what postgraduate qualification they hold in plastic and reconstructive surgery, such as an MCh or DNB in Plastic Surgery, and where they trained. Ask how much of their practice is breast surgery.

3. Ask about experience with your procedure

  • How many of these procedures do you perform each year?
  • What complications have you managed, and how?
  • Can I speak to someone about the process, without being offered testimonials?

4. Professional memberships

Membership of recognised professional societies, such as the Association of Plastic Surgeons of India, can be a positive sign, though it is not a guarantee. Check membership with the society itself.

5. Check the facility

  • Is surgery done in a licensed hospital or day-care facility?
  • Is there a qualified anaesthetist?
  • Is there emergency equipment and arrangements to transfer you to a hospital if needed?

6. Check the product

Ask for the implant manufacturer, model and batch number, and whether it holds approvals in India or with other recognised regulators. You should receive an implant card.

7. Watch for red flags

  • Pressure to book quickly or discounts that expire
  • Guaranteed results or cup-size promises
  • Reluctance to explain risks or show credentials
  • Before-and-after photos that cannot be verified
  • No written consent form or aftercare plan

Key takeaway

A good surgeon welcomes questions, explains risks plainly and gives you time. See breast enlargement safety and the consultation checklist.
